title: HSBC puts $1 million into disaster preparedness in Bangladesh
excerpt: UNICEF, the British Red Cross and Save the Children will run three projects under an 18-month pilot. Districts and reach are not yet public.
content:
HSBC has allocated US$1 million (about Tk 12.43 crore) to three disaster preparedness projects in Bangladesh, run by UNICEF, the British Red Cross with the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society, and Save the Children, The Daily Star reported on 8 November.

The money is part of the bank’s global Disaster Relief Partnership, launched on 13 October with $4.5 million over an 18-month pilot. The Daily Star reported that the pilot also covers Vietnam, Kenya and the Philippines.

What it pays for

  • The projects aim to help communities prepare for emergencies, act early before forecast disasters and protect lives and livelihoods, according to the newspaper.
  • Globally, HSBC says about 40% of the partnership’s funding goes to anticipatory action, such as early warning systems and training for first responders. The rest covers rapid response, pre-positioned supplies and flexible support.
  • Neither HSBC nor the newspaper has said which districts the Bangladesh projects cover, how many people they will reach or how the $1 million is split between the three organisations.

The Bangladesh projects were launched at a ceremony in Dhaka attended by the British High Commission, the newspaper reported.

Why it matters

Anticipatory action, releasing money before a forecast cyclone or flood hits, has been tested in Bangladesh for several years by the UN and the Red Cross Red Crescent movement. Corporate funding for it is still small. The grant is modest, but it is flexible money for preparedness at a time when bilateral aid budgets are falling.

What to watch

Details of the target districts and the number of people covered, and whether the pilot is extended after 18 months.
